Two central themes run through The Due Process of Law. The first is the workings of the various "measures authorised by the law so as to keep the streams of justice pure"--that is to say, contempt of court, judicial inquiries, and powers of arrest and search. The second is the recent development of family law, focusing particularly on Lord Denning's contribution to the law of husband and wife. These broad themes are elaborated through a discussion of Lord Denning's own judgments and opinions on a wide range of topics.

James' Introduction to English Law is a classic of its kind. Presenting the law in its sociological and historical context the book has, over the years, established itself as a concise, succinct guide to the subject. Now thoroughly updated, the book remains invaluable reading for all needing to get to grips with the basic principles. Whether studying law itself, taking other courses with a law element, or just requiring general reading on the intricacies of English law, this book will provide. you with all you need to know.

The book introduces the reader by logical stages to the basic principles of English law, providing a broad perspective that establishes the relationships between the various specialised areas and forms a framework for further study. Each principle is vividly illustrated by interesting cases, and the law is presented in its sociological and historical context. Intended primarily for law students in the early stages of study, the new edition will continue to be of value to other students taking college, university and professional courses involving law.

Covering a variety of law topics and combining theory and cases, this revised edition incorporates the many changes in the field since publication of the previous edition, as well as including a number of new cases. Facts of decided cases are given in detail and key cases are highlighted. The text also contains practical exercises and end-of-chapter questions. This work is designed for non-lawyers taking Law as part of a business or other course.
